reference_sql:
WITH price_points AS (
  SELECT list_price_eur AS price_eur
  FROM price_history
  WHERE product_id = 3
  UNION ALL
  SELECT price_eur
  FROM competitor_prices
  WHERE product_id = 3
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(price_eur), 2) AS avg_price_eur
FROM price_points
alternatives: WITH price_points AS (SELECT product_id, list_price_eur AS price_eur FROM price_history UNION ALL SELECT product_id, price_eur FROM competitor_prices) SELECT ROUND(SUM(price_eur) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_price_eur FROM price_points WHERE product_id = 3

WITH list_prices AS (SELECT SUM(list_price_eur) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM price_history WHERE product_id = 3), checks AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(price_eur), 0) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM competitor_prices WHERE product_id = 3) SELECT ROUND((l.total + c.total) / (l.n + c.n), 2) AS avg_price_eur FROM list_prices l CROSS JOIN checks c

other_way.sql: WITH list_prices AS (SELECT SUM(list_price_eur) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM price_history WHERE product_id = 3), checks AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(price_eur), 0) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM competitor_prices WHERE product_id = 3) SELECT ROUND((l.total + c.total) / (l.n + c.n), 2) AS avg_price_eur FROM list_prices l CROSS JOIN checks c
other_way.tradeoff: Adding up the totals and counts of each table and dividing once avoids the stack, but it is longer and easy to get wrong.
